title: Introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway
takeaway: Vercel will only label an inference provider Audited ZDR after an independent security firm tests its zero data retention claim against code, infrastructure and live traffic and publishes the report, with Baseten, Modal and Wafer as launch partners. If your app sends user prompts or customer data to a model, "we don't keep your data" is becoming something you can check, not just take on trust.

title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
takeaway: Z.ai's new flagship coding model runs a shared block of layers twice to reason more deeply without adding parameters, and the team admits it can get stuck in overly long thinking loops. The API is listed as coming soon and open weights are planned after safety hardening, so treat it as one to watch rather than one to wire into production today.

title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
takeaway: Walmart is rolling out a live Agent Gateway on November 24 that lets Meta's Muse agent buy on a shopper's behalf, through Agent Profiles with spending limits, purchase approvals and a history of what the agent bought. That is a useful pattern to copy: any app that lets an agent take actions needs limits, a human approval step and a visible log.

title: Choose AI Gateway providers by headquarters country
takeaway: AI Gateway can now allowlist or denylist model providers by the country they're headquartered in, team-wide on Pro and Enterprise or per request on any plan. If a client or school asks where their data goes, this turns the answer into a setting, but configure fallback models, because requests fail rather than route to a blocked country.

title: Free Coding Lessons with an AI tutor that won't hand you the answer
takeaway: TU Graz's free Computor site pairs three Python courses and 70 exercises with an AI tutor, Lena, that points out what's off in your code but leaves the fix to you. Vibe coders ship faster when they can read what their agent wrote, and a nudge-not-answer tutor is a low-cost way to build that skill.

title: Vercel Functions now support request bodies up to 20MiB
takeaway: In public beta, Vercel Functions on Node.js, Python and Bun can accept request bodies up to 20MiB instead of 4.5MB, by setting VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_REQUEST_BODY=1 and using the 4GB performance memory setting. If your AI app uploads images, PDFs or audio straight to a function, test this on a preview deployment first, since Edge functions keep the old cap and middleware stops seeing the body.

title: Welcome Inkling 2 Mini, Cutting-edge Performance for your Local Setup
takeaway: Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini is a looped mixture-of-experts model with about 26B total and 3B active parameters, a 1M-token context and image plus text input, with transformers, llama.cpp and MLX support from day one. For builders handling sensitive data, it's a fresh option for prototyping on your own machine, though Hugging Face says more validation is needed.

title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
takeaway: Five memory corruption bugs disclosed in nginx can let an unauthenticated attacker crash a worker or run commands on the server, and a related Linux kernel bug can escalate that to root even from inside a Docker container. If you self-host a shipped app behind nginx on a VPS or in Docker, this is a patch-now event, not a someday task.

title: Catch missing feature flags before they reach production
takeaway: Vercel Flags can now fail a deployment check when a flag exists in your code but was never created in the project, instead of silently falling back to its default value. If your AI agent sprinkles feature flags through a generated app, turn this check on so a half-finished feature can't switch itself on in production.

title: Gemini rebuilds the Eiffel Tower with 32 agents
takeaway: Google had 32 Gemini agents work in parallel from about 70 archival blueprints and photos to generate a construction time-lapse, with the agents checking each other's work against the sources. The builder lesson: multi-agent setups get reliable when every agent is grounded in the same reference material and verifies its peers.

title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
takeaway: With so much code now AI-generated, a wave of companies (Harmonic, Theorem, Axiom Math and &Truth) is using math-style proofs to check that software actually does what it claims. You don't need proofs for a weekend app, but the takeaway scales down: write down what 'correct' means before you prompt, then make the agent prove it with tests.

title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness
takeaway: Hugging Face trained small LoRA adapters that tune an open model to a specific agent harness, lifting Qwen3.8-27B from 39% to 55% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 under the pi harness while cutting average tokens per task from 2.9K to 1.5K. The model is only half the system: the harness you run it in changes both quality and cost.

title: Token fraud is here and it's BAD
takeaway: Claire Vo of ChatPRD describes groups looping free trials and promo codes to resell her product's AI usage or run their own businesses on top of her agent. If you ship an AI app with a free tier, rate limits, signup verification and per-user spend caps belong in version one, not after the first surprise bill.

title: Agents can now find Vercel CLI commands by describing the task
takeaway: `vercel help search "roll back production" --with-help` returns the matching command plus its options, and can also return ready-to-fill `vercel api` calls as JSON. Upgrade the CLI so your coding agent stops guessing deploy commands and looks them up instead.

title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
takeaway: Tool Retrieval, now in preview in the Gemini API, lets an agent work with hundreds of tools while spending fewer tokens on tool definitions. If your app has grown a long list of functions or MCP tools, this is the pattern to watch: load the tools a task needs, not all of them every turn.

title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
takeaway: Google's new mid-tier model is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, with a 1M-token context window and a 95% discount on cached input. For builders, the cached-input price is the story: keep your system prompt and project docs stable so repeat calls hit the cache.

title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
takeaway: GitHub explains the Agent Host Protocol, the open standard that lets a Copilot agent session started in one place keep running and be picked up from another device. Long-running agents are becoming normal, so design your own agent features around sessions that outlive a single browser tab.

title: Inference engineering for software engineers
takeaway: Companies are moving workloads to open models to cut AI spend, with Uber reporting a 50% drop in per-token cost and Pinterest 90%, and notes most teams get there through an inference provider rather than their own GPUs. Once your app has real traffic, the model bill is a product decision: know your cache hit rates, rate limits and tail latency.

title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
takeaway: An agent skill is a versioned folder built around a SKILL.md file that tells any agent when and how to do one repeatable task. Stop re-explaining your deploy steps or brand rules in every chat: write them once as a skill in your repo and every agent you use can follow them.

title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
takeaway: The Verge's Stepback column looks at people using large language models to hack and customize their own hardware, something that used to take deep expertise. Vibe coding is leaving the browser: the same idea-to-working-thing loop now applies to TVs, cameras and the devices around you.
